data.title: Scotland v Slovenia: Key stats - Yahoo Sports
data.content: * Scotland have never lost against Slovenia in six previous meetings (W2 D4), keeping four clean sheets. * Slovenia have never scored an away goal against Scotland, drawing 0-0 in September 2004 and losing 1-0 in March 2017, both times in World Cup qualifiers. * Scotland were beaten 3-0 by Switzerland in their last home game - they haven't lost back-to-back competitive home games since June 2019 when they were defeated by Russia and Belgium. * Slovenia have just two wins in their past 13 matches in all competitions (D6 L5), with defeats in four of their past seven away games (W1 D2). * Scotland have won seven of their past eight matches against nations outside the top 50 of the Fifa rankings at the time of the game (D1), while they are unbeaten in their past 17 competitive games against those nations (W14 D3). * Scotland have received a red card in each of their past two matches, as many as their previous 122 games combined.

data.title: Scotland: Sebastian Pocognoli’s ‘sad’ Hampden debut as he demands Nations League response - Sky Sports
data.content: Jack Hendry was sent off in the 3-0 defeat to Switzerland, while Scotland have failed to score in their last four games; they travel to North Macedonia in their next Nations League match on Saturday before hosting Slovenia three days later. "Even with 11 men, if we had the bad result, we would have wanted to give something, some emotion, something to analyse, something to give a direction about where we want to go, and we didn't have the chance to show it and that frustrated me a lot.". With just one point and no goals from their opening two Nations League fixtures after a 0-0 draw in Slovenia at the weekend, Pocognoli admits Scotland's next match in North Macedonia on Saturday has taken on added significance. Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn insists they will win and lose as a team after Jack Hendry tried to apologise for his red card in their Nations League defeat to Switzerland.
